Stagger entrance: each card fades in with 80ms delay - Hover: subtle lift (translateY(-2px)) + shadow increase - Intersection Observer trigger at 20% visibility Responsive Collapse: Desktop: 3-column bento grid Tablet (md): 2-column, large items span full width Mobile (sm): single column, all items equal size ``` **Best for:** Feature sections, capability showcases, dashboard previews **Niches:** SaaS/Tech, AI/ML, Developer Tools, Analytics ### Pattern 2: Asymmetric Split Layout **What:** 60/40 or 70/30 content split, alternating sides per section. ``` Structure: Row 1: Text (60%) | Visual (40%) -- text-left Row 2: Visual (40%) | Text (60%) -- text-right (alternating) Row 3: Text (60%) | Visual (40%) -- text-left Implementation: grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-5 gap-8 lg:gap-12 items-center Text side: lg:col-span-3 Visual side: lg:col-span-2 Alternating: use flex-row-reverse on even rows (desktop only) Visual Rules: - Text side: heading + description + bullet list or mini-features + CTA - Visual side: product screenshot, illustration, code snippet, or video embed - Vertical alignment: items-center - Section padding: py-20 md:py-28 Animation: - Text: slide in from left (or right for alternate rows), 400ms - Visual: slide in from right (or left), 400ms, 150ms delay - Trigger: Intersection Observer at 30% visibility Responsive: Desktop: 60/40 split Tablet: 55/45 split Mobile: stacked vertically, visual above text ``` **Best for:** Feature deep-dives, how-it-works, product showcases **Niches:** All niches (universal pattern, adapt visual treatment per niche) ### Pattern 3: Gradient CTA Sections **What:** Full-width call-to-action sections with gradient backgrounds. ``` Structure: Full-width section with gradient bg Centered content: heading + description + dual buttons Optional: floating decorative elements (shapes, patterns) Implementation: bg-gradient-to-br from-primary via-primary/80 to-secondary Dark: from-primary/20 via-background to-secondary/20 (muted) Content: text-center max-w-3xl mx-auto Visual Rules: - Gradient should feel intentional, not random - Text on gradient: always white or very light (contrast check!) - Primary CTA: solid white bg, dark text (inverted from gradient) - Secondary CTA: ghost button, white border, white text - Padding: py-20 md:py-28 - Optional grain/noise overlay: opacity-5 for texture Animation: - Gradient subtle shift on scroll (background-position animation) - CTA buttons: hover scale(1.02) + shadow increase - Text: fade-in-up entrance Performance: - Gradients as CSS only, never images - No backdrop-blur on CTA sections (keep it fast) ``` **Best for:** Final CTA before footer, mid-page conversion pushes **Niches:** All (adjust gradient colors to niche palette) ### Pattern 4: Glassmorphism Cards **What:** Frosted glass effect cards with translucent backgrounds and blur. ``` Implementation: bg-white/10 dark:bg-white/5 backdrop-blur-md (12px) border border-white/20 dark:border-white/10 rounded-xl p-6 Visual Rules: - MAX 5 glassmorphism elements per page (performance!) - Best on gradient or image backgrounds where blur is visible - Add subtle inner shadow for depth: shadow-inner shadow-white/5 - Text on glass: high contrast (white on dark glass, dark on light glass) - Glass card content: icon + heading + description Performance (STRICT): - backdrop-blur is GPU-intensive - Max 5 elements with backdrop-blur per viewport - Fallback for unsupported browsers: solid bg with opacity - @supports not (backdrop-filter: blur(12px)) { bg-slate-800/90 } - Use will-change: transform on glass cards Animation: - Subtle border glow on hover (border-color transition) - Card lift on hover: translateY(-4px) 200ms - No blur animation (too expensive) Dark mode: - Glass cards look better on dark backgrounds - Light mode: bg-white/60 backdrop-blur-sm (lighter blur) - Dark mode: bg-white/5 backdrop-blur-md (heavier blur) ``` **Best for:** Feature cards on gradient backgrounds, pricing cards, testimonials **Niches:** AI/ML, Creative/Agency, Gaming (avoid for Enterprise, Healthcare) ### Pattern 5: Animated Number Counters **What:** Statistics that animate from 0 to target value when scrolled into view. ``` Implementation (React hook): useCountAnimation(targetValue, duration, startOnView) - Uses requestAnimationFrame for smooth 60fps - Spring easing (fast start, slow finish) - Intersection Observer triggers at 50% visibility - Runs once only (ref flag) Display: Metrics bar: flex items-center justify-center gap-8 md:gap-16 Each metric:
{count}+ {label}
Visual Rules: - 3-5 metrics in a row (not more) - Large numbers: font-bold, text-primary or text-foreground - Labels: text-muted-foreground, text-sm - Dividers between metrics (optional): border-r border-border - Format numbers: 1000 -> "1K+", 1000000 -> "1M+" - Include suffix: "+", "%", "x", "K", "M" Animation: - Duration: 1500-2000ms per counter - Easing: easeOutExpo (fast start, smooth landing) - Stagger: 100ms between each counter - Reduced motion: show final numbers instantly, no animation Performance: - requestAnimationFrame only (no setInterval) - Cleanup on unmount - Single Intersection Observer instance for all counters ``` **Best for:** Social proof sections, hero sections, trust bars **Niches:** All niches (universal pattern) ### Pattern 6: Parallax Hero **What:** Depth-creating scroll effect where background moves slower than foreground. ``` Implementation: CSS transform approach (NOT scroll hijacking): - Background layer: transform: translateY(calc(var(--scroll) * 0.15)) - Foreground: normal scroll - Set --scroll via requestAnimationFrame scroll listener OR Framer Motion: - useScroll() + useTransform() - transformTemplate for GPU-accelerated transforms Visual Rules: - Parallax speed: 0.1-0.2 (subtle, not nauseating) - Background: gradient, abstract pattern, or blurred image - Foreground: text content + CTA - Floating elements at different speeds for depth layers - Max 3 parallax layers (background, mid, foreground) Performance (STRICT): - transform: translate3d() only (GPU composited) - Never animate top/left/margin (triggers layout) - will-change: transform on parallax elements - Disable entirely on mobile (performance + motion sensitivity) - Use requestAnimationFrame, never scroll event directly Reduced Motion: - @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): disable all parallax - Static positioned elements instead - Content still readable and functional Responsive: Desktop: full parallax with floating elements Tablet: reduced parallax (speed 0.05-0.1) Mobile: disabled -- static hero layout ``` **Best for:** Hero sections, full-page backgrounds **Niches:** AI/ML, Creative/Agency, Premium SaaS (skip for data-heavy/Enterprise) ### Pattern 7: Mega-Footer **What:** Information-rich footer with multiple columns, newsletter CTA, and social links. ``` Structure:
Heading + Email input + Subscribe button
Column 1: Brand logo + tagline + social icons Column 2: Product (links) Column 3: Company (links) Column 4: Resources (links) Column 5: Legal (links)
Copyright + Legal links + Theme toggle
Visual Rules: - Background: slate-950 (always dark, regardless of page theme) - Links: text-white/60 hover:text-white transition - Column headings: text-sm font-semibold text-white uppercase tracking-wider - Social icons: 20x20px, text-white/40 hover:text-white - Newsletter input: bg-white/10 border-white/20 text-white placeholder:text-white/40 - Max 5 columns on desktop, 2 on mobile - Mobile: columns collapse to 2-column grid, then accordion for 5+ columns Animation: - Links: color transition 150ms - Social icons: scale(1.1) on hover - Newsletter button: bg color transition - No entrance animation (footer is below fold, not impactful) ``` **Best for:** All page types (every page needs a footer) **Niches:** All niches (universal, adjust column content per product) ### Pattern 8: Dark Mode Pricing **What:** Pricing tables optimized for dark backgrounds with gradient accents. ``` Structure: Section: py-20 md:py-28 Toggle: Monthly / Annual (with "Save X%" badge) Cards: grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-6 md:gap-8 Featured Plan Visual Treatment: - Scale: scale-105 on desktop (larger than siblings) - Border: gradient border (from-primary to-secondary) - Badge: "Most Popular" pill at top - Glow: box-shadow: 0 0 60px var(--primary) / 0.15 - Background: subtle gradient overlay Visual Rules (Dark Mode): - Card bg: bg-white/5 dark:bg-white/5 (glass-like) - Featured: bg-primary/10 border-primary/30 - Divider between price and features: border-white/10 - Check icons: text-primary (colored) - X icons (excluded features): text-muted-foreground/50 - CTA: featured plan gets solid primary button, others get ghost/outline Visual Rules (Light Mode): - Card bg: bg-white border shadow-sm - Featured: bg-primary/5 border-primary ring-1 ring-primary/20 - Standard elevation hierarchy Toggle Implementation: - Pill-style toggle with bg-primary sliding indicator - Annual price: show monthly equivalent with "billed annually" note - Discount badge: bg-green-500/10 text-green-500 "Save 20%" Responsive: Desktop: 3 cards side-by-side, featured scaled up Tablet: 3 cards, no scale, equal size Mobile: stacked vertically, featured has top border accent ``` **Best for:** Pricing pages, landing page pricing sections **Niches:** All (adjust card count and style per pricing model) ### Pattern 9: Testimonial Carousel **What:** Rotating customer testimonials with auto-play and manual controls. ``` Structure: Section heading: "What our customers say" or niche-specific Carousel container with overflow-hidden Navigation: dots + arrows Auto-play with pause-on-hover Card Content: - Star rating (1-5 stars, yellow-400/amber-400) - Quote text (2-4 sentences) - Avatar image (48x48 rounded-full) - Name (font-semibold) - Role + Company (text-muted-foreground text-sm) - Optional: company logo Visual Rules: - Quote text: text-lg md:text-xl, slightly italic or normal weight - Opening quote mark: text-6xl text-primary/20 decorative (optional) - Card: bg-card rounded-xl p-6 md:p-8 border - Desktop: show 3 cards visible at once - Tablet: show 2 cards - Mobile: show 1 card, swipeable Animation: - Slide transition: 400ms ease-out - Auto-play: 5 second interval - Pause on hover AND on focus (accessibility) - Dot indicator: bg-primary for active, bg-muted for inactive - Entrance: fade-in-up for entire section Accessibility: - role="region" aria-label="Customer testimonials" - aria-roledescription="carousel" - Each slide: role="group" aria-roledescription="slide" - Previous/Next buttons: aria-label="Previous/Next testimonial" - Auto-play: pause button with aria-label="Pause auto-play" - Reduced motion: no slide animation, instant switch Alternative Layout (Grid, no carousel): grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6 All testimonials visible. Better for 3-6 testimonials. Use carousel only for 6+ testimonials. ``` **Best for:** Social proof sections on landing pages, about pages **Niches:** All niches (adjust quote style per audience) ### Pattern 10: Micro-Interaction Buttons **What:** Buttons with satisfying, purposeful feedback animations. ``` Hover Effects (pick per niche): 1. Scale + Shadow Lift: hover:scale-[1.02] hover:shadow-lg active:scale-[0.98] transition-all duration-200 2. Gradient Shift: bg-gradient-to-r from-primary to-secondary hover:from-secondary hover:to-primary transition-all duration-300 3. Fill Sweep (left to right): relative overflow-hidden before:absolute before:inset-0 before:bg-primary before:translate-x-[-100%] hover:before:translate-x-0 before:transition-transform before:duration-300 4. Icon Animation: group flex items-center gap-2 Arrow icon: group-hover:translate-x-1 transition-transform duration-200 5. Glow Effect (dark mode): hover:shadow-[0_0_20px_var(--primary)/30] transition-shadow duration-300 6. Underline Sweep: relative after:absolute after:bottom-0 after:left-0 after:h-0.5 after:w-0 hover:after:w-full after:bg-primary after:transition-all after:duration-300 Press Feedback: - active:scale-[0.98] on all buttons (tactile feel) - Duration: 100ms (snappy) Loading State: - Replace text with spinner (Loader2 icon, animate-spin) - Maintain button width (min-w to prevent layout shift) - disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed Niche Mapping: Tech/Dev: Scale + Shadow (professional, satisfying) Creative/Agency: Gradient Shift or Fill Sweep (dramatic) Enterprise: Scale + Shadow only (conservative) AI/ML: Glow Effect + Scale (futuristic) E-commerce: Icon Animation (clear directional CTA) ``` **Best for:** All CTAs, navigation actions, form submissions **Niches:** All (select effect per niche mood) --- ## Section 4: Visual Effects Performance Rules ### Gradients - Max 3 gradient elements per viewport - CSS gradients only (never image gradients for solid colors) - Avoid gradient on gradient (visual noise) - Dark mode: reduce gradient intensity by 30-50% - `bg-gradient-to-br` preferred over radial for performance ### Glassmorphism (backdrop-blur) - **Hard limit: 5 elements with backdrop-blur per page** - Fallback: `@supports not (backdrop-filter: blur(12px)) { solid bg with opacity }` - Use `will-change: transform` on glass elements - Never stack glass on glass (blur compounds, GPU thrashes) - Mobile: reduce blur from `backdrop-blur-md` to `backdrop-blur-sm` ### Glow Effects - `box-shadow` with brand color at 15-25% opacity - Dark mode: increase to 20-30% (more visible) - Max 3 glow elements per viewport - Never animate box-shadow spread (expensive) -- only animate opacity ### Grain/Noise Textures - CSS-only using SVG filter: `url("data:image/svg+xml,...")` with `opacity-[0.03]` - Must not affect LCP (applied as pseudo-element, not on content) - Hide on `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` - Never use raster noise images (file size) ### General Rules - `will-change`: use sparingly, only on elements that actually animate - `contain: paint` on sections with heavy effects (prevent paint leak) - `transform: translate3d(0,0,0)` to force GPU layer (use for scroll animations) - `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: remove all transform-based animations, keep opacity-only transitions - Test on mid-range Android device (not just M-series MacBook)

# Flowbase Design DNA -- Pixel's Visual Intelligence > 9 collection profiles + niche mapping + 10 mandatory patterns + performance rules. > This file is the core of Pixel's design differentiation. > Load whenever designing any public-facing page. --- ## Section 1: Collection DNA Profiles Each Flowbase collection has a distinct visual personality. Pixel blends collections based on niche -- never uses one collection at 100%. ### 1. Breeze -- Light, Airy, SaaS-Friendly ``` Mood: Calm, trustworthy, approachable Background: White (#FFFFFF) with subtle off-white sections (#FAFAFA) Color: Soft blues, greens, lavenders as accents. Pastel tints. Typography: Rounded sans-serif headings (Plus Jakarta Sans, Nunito). Clean body (Inter). Spacing: Generous -- 32-48px component gaps, 80-120px section padding Corners: Rounded-xl to rounded-2xl (12-16px) Shadows: Soft, diffused -- shadow-sm to shadow-md with blue/purple tint Animation: Gentle -- 300-400ms fades, subtle hover lifts, no parallax Photography: Light, bright, lifestyle. Soft focus backgrounds. Icons: Rounded stroke icons (Lucide, Phosphor) Dark mode: Slate-900 base, muted accent colors, reduced shadow intensity Layout: Symmetric grids, centered alignment, comfortable density Best for: Health tech, lifestyle SaaS, consumer apps, wellness, food/beverage Avoid for: Developer tools, analytics dashboards, security products ``` ### 2. Chalk -- Minimal, Text-Forward, Editorial ``` Mood: Intellectual, clean, developer-friendly Background: Pure white or very light gray. Minimal color. Color: Monochrome primary. One accent color max (often blue or green). Typography: Tight, deliberate. Geist/Inter headings at large sizes, tight tracking. Strong typographic hierarchy. Type IS the design. Spacing: Disciplined -- consistent 24-32px gaps, generous line-height Corners: Sharp to slightly rounded (0-8px). Clean geometry. Shadows: Almost none. Relies on borders and whitespace for separation. Animation: Minimal -- subtle fades only. Content speaks, not motion. Photography: Rarely used. When used: stark, high-contrast, editorial. Icons: Thin stroke, consistent weight (Lucide default). Dark mode: Zinc-950 base, pure white text, borders for structure Layout: Strong vertical rhythm, left-aligned or centered, grid-disciplined Best for: Developer tools, documentation, content platforms, API products Avoid for: Consumer apps, playful brands, visual-heavy products ``` ### 3. Prism -- Colorful, Gradient-Rich, Bold ``` Mood: Energetic, futuristic, innovative Background: Deep darks (slate-950, zinc-950) OR vibrant gradient washes Color: Multi-color gradients (purple-blue-pink, cyan-green-yellow). Vibrant, saturated. Neon accents on dark backgrounds. Typography: Bold geometric headings (Space Grotesk, Syne). Large display sizes. Weight 700-800 for impact. Spacing: Medium-generous -- 24-40px gaps, dramatic section spacing Corners: Mixed -- rounded-lg for cards, rounded-full for badges/pills Shadows: Glow effects -- box-shadow with color opacity (shadow-primary/20) Animation: Heavy -- gradient shifts, glassmorphism hover, particle effects, animated backgrounds, text reveals, staggered entrances Photography: Rarely -- abstract patterns, data visualizations, gradient meshes Icons: Filled or duotone icons with gradient fills Dark mode: Native dark (dark IS the primary mode). Light variant: white + muted gradients. Layout: Asymmetric, overlapping elements, bento grids, broken conventions Best for: AI/ML products, creative tools, marketing platforms, gaming, crypto Avoid for: Healthcare, legal, government, enterprise B2B ``` ### 4. Aspect -- Clean, Structured, Professional ``` Mood: Trustworthy, capable, enterprise-ready Background: White primary, gray-50 alternating sections Color: Neutral base (slate/gray) + one strong brand accent. Conservative palette. Typography: Professional sans-serif (Inter, DM Sans). Moderate heading sizes. Clear hierarchy without drama. Spacing: Balanced -- 24-32px gaps, 64-96px section padding Corners: Rounded-md to rounded-lg (6-12px). Consistent, not dramatic. Shadows: Medium -- shadow-sm for cards, shadow-md on hover. Neutral tints. Animation: Subtle -- 200-300ms transitions, hover shadows, smooth reveals Photography: Professional team photos, office environments, product screenshots Icons: Clean outline icons, consistent 24px size (Lucide, Heroicons) Dark mode: Slate-900 base, maintained professional tone, no neon Layout: Strong grid alignment, 12-column base, consistent card sizes Best for: Enterprise B2B, fintech, project management, HR/recruiting, CRM Avoid for: Gaming, creative agencies, consumer entertainment ``` ### 5. Haus -- Architectural, Geometric, Premium ``` Mood: Premium, intentional, design-conscious Background: Near-black (#0A0A0A) or warm whites (#FAFAF8). Dramatic contrast. Color: Muted earth tones OR monochrome + one bold accent. Warm: amber, terracotta, sage. Cool: slate, steel. Typography: Display typefaces at extreme sizes (72-120px headings). Strong weight contrast (300 body, 800 heading). Tight tracking. Spacing: Dramatic -- 48-64px component gaps, 120-160px section padding. Whitespace as design element. Corners: Varies by element -- rounded-none for hero images, rounded-2xl for cards Shadows: Dramatic -- large spread, soft blur. Dark mode: subtle glow. Animation: Sophisticated -- parallax, scroll-driven reveals, GSAP-style sequences, magnetic hover effects, smooth page transitions Photography: High-end architectural, fashion-inspired, dramatic lighting Icons: Custom SVG or minimal outline. Oversized when used. Dark mode: Dark IS the brand (dark-first). Light: warm white with muted tones. Layout: Asymmetric, large negative space, broken grid, full-bleed images Best for: Design agencies, premium SaaS, architecture/real estate, luxury brands Avoid for: Budget tools, data-heavy apps, developer docs ``` ### 6. Apex -- Data-Forward, Dense, Powerful ``` Mood: Technical, authoritative, data-rich Background: Dark-first (slate-950, navy-950). Dense information display. Color: Neon accents (cyan, green, amber) on dark backgrounds. Data visualization colors. Monochrome text hierarchy. Typography: System or mono-influenced (JetBrains Mono, Fira Code for data). Compact body text. Dense tables and metrics. Spacing: Compact -- 16-24px gaps, 48-64px section padding. Information-dense. Corners: Small -- rounded-sm to rounded-md. Functional, not decorative. Shadows: Minimal. Borders and background shifts for separation. Animation: Data animations -- counter roll-ups, chart animations, live data feeds, real-time ticker effects. Functional motion, not decorative. Photography: Almost never. Dashboards, charts, code snippets instead. Icons: Small, functional. Phosphor or custom SVG. Dark mode: Native dark. Light variant: off-white with maintained density. Layout: Multi-column, card-dense, metric grids, data tables Best for: Analytics, monitoring, trading platforms, DevOps, infrastructure Avoid for: Consumer products, lifestyle, education (too dense for casual users) ``` ### 7. Terrace -- Warm, Approachable, Community ``` Mood: Friendly, inclusive, community-driven Background: Warm whites (#FFFBF5, #FFF7ED), cream tones Color: Warm palette: coral, amber, warm purple, sage green. Approachable, not corporate. Slightly muted saturation. Typography: Rounded, friendly fonts (Plus Jakarta Sans, Quicksand headings). Generous line-height. Comfortable reading. Spacing: Generous -- 32-48px gaps, 80-120px sections. Breathable. Corners: Very rounded -- rounded-xl to rounded-2xl. Soft, pillowy. Shadows: Warm tinted -- shadow with orange/amber opacity. Soft and diffused. Animation: Playful -- bouncy micro-interactions, emoji reactions, confetti on success, spring physics on buttons Photography: Diverse people, community events, user-generated content feel. Authentic, not stock-photo-perfect. Icons: Rounded, filled or duotone. Warm colors. Phosphor rounded. Dark mode: Warm dark: zinc-900 with amber undertones, maintained warmth Layout: Card-based, rounded containers, comfortable density Best for: Marketplaces, community platforms, education, social tools, non-profits Avoid for: Enterprise, security/compliance, developer tools ``` ### 8. Alley -- Urban, Creative, Unconventional ``` Mood: Edgy, creative, rule-breaking Background: High contrast -- pure black or pure white. No middle ground. Color: Bold, unexpected combinations. Neon on black. Warm on cool. Color blocks as design elements. Intentionally clashing. Typography: Oversized, statement headings (80-200px). Mixed weights in same line. All-caps for impact. Compressed or extended widths. Spacing: Intentionally uneven. Tight in some areas, vast in others. Tension through spacing contrast. Corners: Mixed extremes -- rounded-none and rounded-full on same page. Shadows: Hard shadows (offset, no blur) or neon glow. Not soft corporate. Animation: Scroll-triggered reveals, text marquees, horizontal scroll sections, cursor interactions, GSAP timeline sequences, glitch effects Photography: Editorial, high-contrast, grainy. Street photography aesthetic. Black and white mixed with color pops. Icons: Custom SVG, hand-drawn feel, or no icons (typography carries weight). Dark mode: Black-first. White variant: stark, high-contrast. Layout: Broken grids, overlapping elements, horizontal scroll sections, magazine-style layouts, full-bleed typography Best for: Creative agencies, startups (brand-forward), music, fashion, media Avoid for: Enterprise, healthcare, finance, government (too unconventional) ``` ### 9. Noda -- Modular, System-Focused, Technical ``` Mood: Systematic, developer-friendly, modern technical Background: Dark: zinc-950 with subtle grid patterns. Light: white with dotted grid. Color: Blue-violet primary, cyan/green accents. Code-inspired color palette. Syntax-highlighting-influenced accent colors. Typography: Modern geometric (Geist Sans, Inter). Mono for technical content. Clean hierarchy. Code snippets prominent. Spacing: Systematic -- 8px base grid, consistent 24-32px gaps Corners: Rounded-lg consistently. Card-based system. Shadows: Subtle borders + slight shadow. Dark: border-white/10 + glow. Animation: Functional -- code typing effects, terminal animations, API response simulations, tab switching, smooth state transitions Photography: Rare. Product screenshots, terminal UIs, code editors instead. Icons: System icons, consistent stroke weight. Lucide default. Dark mode: Polished in both modes. Dark: rich with colored borders. Light: clean. Layout: Bento grid, modular cards, tabbed interfaces, code-alongside-UI Best for: Developer tools, API products, infrastructure, SaaS platforms, DevEx Avoid for: Lifestyle brands, visual-heavy consumer products ``` --- ## Section 2: Niche-to-Collection Mapping Table Use this table to determine the collection blend for any niche. Stagger entrance: each card fades in with 80ms delay - Hover: subtle lift (translateY(-2px)) + shadow increase - Intersection Observer trigger at 20% visibility Responsive Collapse: Desktop: 3-column bento grid Tablet (md): 2-column, large items span full width Mobile (sm): single column, all items equal size ``` **Best for:** Feature sections, capability showcases, dashboard previews **Niches:** SaaS/Tech, AI/ML, Developer Tools, Analytics ### Pattern 2: Asymmetric Split Layout **What:** 60/40 or 70/30 content split, alternating sides per section. ``` Structure: Row 1: Text (60%) | Visual (40%) -- text-left Row 2: Visual (40%) | Text (60%) -- text-right (alternating) Row 3: Text (60%) | Visual (40%) -- text-left Implementation: grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-5 gap-8 lg:gap-12 items-center Text side: lg:col-span-3 Visual side: lg:col-span-2 Alternating: use flex-row-reverse on even rows (desktop only) Visual Rules: - Text side: heading + description + bullet list or mini-features + CTA - Visual side: product screenshot, illustration, code snippet, or video embed - Vertical alignment: items-center - Section padding: py-20 md:py-28 Animation: - Text: slide in from left (or right for alternate rows), 400ms - Visual: slide in from right (or left), 400ms, 150ms delay - Trigger: Intersection Observer at 30% visibility Responsive: Desktop: 60/40 split Tablet: 55/45 split Mobile: stacked vertically, visual above text ``` **Best for:** Feature deep-dives, how-it-works, product showcases **Niches:** All niches (universal pattern, adapt visual treatment per niche) ### Pattern 3: Gradient CTA Sections **What:** Full-width call-to-action sections with gradient backgrounds. ``` Structure: Full-width section with gradient bg Centered content: heading + description + dual buttons Optional: floating decorative elements (shapes, patterns) Implementation: bg-gradient-to-br from-primary via-primary/80 to-secondary Dark: from-primary/20 via-background to-secondary/20 (muted) Content: text-center max-w-3xl mx-auto Visual Rules: - Gradient should feel intentional, not random - Text on gradient: always white or very light (contrast check!) - Primary CTA: solid white bg, dark text (inverted from gradient) - Secondary CTA: ghost button, white border, white text - Padding: py-20 md:py-28 - Optional grain/noise overlay: opacity-5 for texture Animation: - Gradient subtle shift on scroll (background-position animation) - CTA buttons: hover scale(1.02) + shadow increase - Text: fade-in-up entrance Performance: - Gradients as CSS only, never images - No backdrop-blur on CTA sections (keep it fast) ``` **Best for:** Final CTA before footer, mid-page conversion pushes **Niches:** All (adjust gradient colors to niche palette) ### Pattern 4: Glassmorphism Cards **What:** Frosted glass effect cards with translucent backgrounds and blur. ``` Implementation: bg-white/10 dark:bg-white/5 backdrop-blur-md (12px) border border-white/20 dark:border-white/10 rounded-xl p-6 Visual Rules: - MAX 5 glassmorphism elements per page (performance!) - Best on gradient or image backgrounds where blur is visible - Add subtle inner shadow for depth: shadow-inner shadow-white/5 - Text on glass: high contrast (white on dark glass, dark on light glass) - Glass card content: icon + heading + description Performance (STRICT): - backdrop-blur is GPU-intensive - Max 5 elements with backdrop-blur per viewport - Fallback for unsupported browsers: solid bg with opacity - @supports not (backdrop-filter: blur(12px)) { bg-slate-800/90 } - Use will-change: transform on glass cards Animation: - Subtle border glow on hover (border-color transition) - Card lift on hover: translateY(-4px) 200ms - No blur animation (too expensive) Dark mode: - Glass cards look better on dark backgrounds - Light mode: bg-white/60 backdrop-blur-sm (lighter blur) - Dark mode: bg-white/5 backdrop-blur-md (heavier blur) ``` **Best for:** Feature cards on gradient backgrounds, pricing cards, testimonials **Niches:** AI/ML, Creative/Agency, Gaming (avoid for Enterprise, Healthcare) ### Pattern 5: Animated Number Counters **What:** Statistics that animate from 0 to target value when scrolled into view. ``` Implementation (React hook): useCountAnimation(targetValue, duration, startOnView) - Uses requestAnimationFrame for smooth 60fps - Spring easing (fast start, slow finish) - Intersection Observer triggers at 50% visibility - Runs once only (ref flag) Display: Metrics bar: flex items-center justify-center gap-8 md:gap-16 Each metric:
{count}+ {label}
Visual Rules: - 3-5 metrics in a row (not more) - Large numbers: font-bold, text-primary or text-foreground - Labels: text-muted-foreground, text-sm - Dividers between metrics (optional): border-r border-border - Format numbers: 1000 -> "1K+", 1000000 -> "1M+" - Include suffix: "+", "%", "x", "K", "M" Animation: - Duration: 1500-2000ms per counter - Easing: easeOutExpo (fast start, smooth landing) - Stagger: 100ms between each counter - Reduced motion: show final numbers instantly, no animation Performance: - requestAnimationFrame only (no setInterval) - Cleanup on unmount - Single Intersection Observer instance for all counters ``` **Best for:** Social proof sections, hero sections, trust bars **Niches:** All niches (universal pattern) ### Pattern 6: Parallax Hero **What:** Depth-creating scroll effect where background moves slower than foreground. ``` Implementation: CSS transform approach (NOT scroll hijacking): - Background layer: transform: translateY(calc(var(--scroll) * 0.15)) - Foreground: normal scroll - Set --scroll via requestAnimationFrame scroll listener OR Framer Motion: - useScroll() + useTransform() - transformTemplate for GPU-accelerated transforms Visual Rules: - Parallax speed: 0.1-0.2 (subtle, not nauseating) - Background: gradient, abstract pattern, or blurred image - Foreground: text content + CTA - Floating elements at different speeds for depth layers - Max 3 parallax layers (background, mid, foreground) Performance (STRICT): - transform: translate3d() only (GPU composited) - Never animate top/left/margin (triggers layout) - will-change: transform on parallax elements - Disable entirely on mobile (performance + motion sensitivity) - Use requestAnimationFrame, never scroll event directly Reduced Motion: - @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): disable all parallax - Static positioned elements instead - Content still readable and functional Responsive: Desktop: full parallax with floating elements Tablet: reduced parallax (speed 0.05-0.1) Mobile: disabled -- static hero layout ``` **Best for:** Hero sections, full-page backgrounds **Niches:** AI/ML, Creative/Agency, Premium SaaS (skip for data-heavy/Enterprise) ### Pattern 7: Mega-Footer **What:** Information-rich footer with multiple columns, newsletter CTA, and social links. ``` Structure:
Heading + Email input + Subscribe button
Column 1: Brand logo + tagline + social icons Column 2: Product (links) Column 3: Company (links) Column 4: Resources (links) Column 5: Legal (links)
Copyright + Legal links + Theme toggle
Visual Rules: - Background: slate-950 (always dark, regardless of page theme) - Links: text-white/60 hover:text-white transition - Column headings: text-sm font-semibold text-white uppercase tracking-wider - Social icons: 20x20px, text-white/40 hover:text-white - Newsletter input: bg-white/10 border-white/20 text-white placeholder:text-white/40 - Max 5 columns on desktop, 2 on mobile - Mobile: columns collapse to 2-column grid, then accordion for 5+ columns Animation: - Links: color transition 150ms - Social icons: scale(1.1) on hover - Newsletter button: bg color transition - No entrance animation (footer is below fold, not impactful) ``` **Best for:** All page types (every page needs a footer) **Niches:** All niches (universal, adjust column content per product) ### Pattern 8: Dark Mode Pricing **What:** Pricing tables optimized for dark backgrounds with gradient accents. ``` Structure: Section: py-20 md:py-28 Toggle: Monthly / Annual (with "Save X%" badge) Cards: grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-6 md:gap-8 Featured Plan Visual Treatment: - Scale: scale-105 on desktop (larger than siblings) - Border: gradient border (from-primary to-secondary) - Badge: "Most Popular" pill at top - Glow: box-shadow: 0 0 60px var(--primary) / 0.15 - Background: subtle gradient overlay Visual Rules (Dark Mode): - Card bg: bg-white/5 dark:bg-white/5 (glass-like) - Featured: bg-primary/10 border-primary/30 - Divider between price and features: border-white/10 - Check icons: text-primary (colored) - X icons (excluded features): text-muted-foreground/50 - CTA: featured plan gets solid primary button, others get ghost/outline Visual Rules (Light Mode): - Card bg: bg-white border shadow-sm - Featured: bg-primary/5 border-primary ring-1 ring-primary/20 - Standard elevation hierarchy Toggle Implementation: - Pill-style toggle with bg-primary sliding indicator - Annual price: show monthly equivalent with "billed annually" note - Discount badge: bg-green-500/10 text-green-500 "Save 20%" Responsive: Desktop: 3 cards side-by-side, featured scaled up Tablet: 3 cards, no scale, equal size Mobile: stacked vertically, featured has top border accent ``` **Best for:** Pricing pages, landing page pricing sections **Niches:** All (adjust card count and style per pricing model) ### Pattern 9: Testimonial Carousel **What:** Rotating customer testimonials with auto-play and manual controls. ``` Structure: Section heading: "What our customers say" or niche-specific Carousel container with overflow-hidden Navigation: dots + arrows Auto-play with pause-on-hover Card Content: - Star rating (1-5 stars, yellow-400/amber-400) - Quote text (2-4 sentences) - Avatar image (48x48 rounded-full) - Name (font-semibold) - Role + Company (text-muted-foreground text-sm) - Optional: company logo Visual Rules: - Quote text: text-lg md:text-xl, slightly italic or normal weight - Opening quote mark: text-6xl text-primary/20 decorative (optional) - Card: bg-card rounded-xl p-6 md:p-8 border - Desktop: show 3 cards visible at once - Tablet: show 2 cards - Mobile: show 1 card, swipeable Animation: - Slide transition: 400ms ease-out - Auto-play: 5 second interval - Pause on hover AND on focus (accessibility) - Dot indicator: bg-primary for active, bg-muted for inactive - Entrance: fade-in-up for entire section Accessibility: - role="region" aria-label="Customer testimonials" - aria-roledescription="carousel" - Each slide: role="group" aria-roledescription="slide" - Previous/Next buttons: aria-label="Previous/Next testimonial" - Auto-play: pause button with aria-label="Pause auto-play" - Reduced motion: no slide animation, instant switch Alternative Layout (Grid, no carousel): grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6 All testimonials visible. Better for 3-6 testimonials. Use carousel only for 6+ testimonials. ``` **Best for:** Social proof sections on landing pages, about pages **Niches:** All niches (adjust quote style per audience) ### Pattern 10: Micro-Interaction Buttons **What:** Buttons with satisfying, purposeful feedback animations. ``` Hover Effects (pick per niche): 1. Scale + Shadow Lift: hover:scale-[1.02] hover:shadow-lg active:scale-[0.98] transition-all duration-200 2. Gradient Shift: bg-gradient-to-r from-primary to-secondary hover:from-secondary hover:to-primary transition-all duration-300 3. Fill Sweep (left to right): relative overflow-hidden before:absolute before:inset-0 before:bg-primary before:translate-x-[-100%] hover:before:translate-x-0 before:transition-transform before:duration-300 4. Icon Animation: group flex items-center gap-2 Arrow icon: group-hover:translate-x-1 transition-transform duration-200 5. Glow Effect (dark mode): hover:shadow-[0_0_20px_var(--primary)/30] transition-shadow duration-300 6. Underline Sweep: relative after:absolute after:bottom-0 after:left-0 after:h-0.5 after:w-0 hover:after:w-full after:bg-primary after:transition-all after:duration-300 Press Feedback: - active:scale-[0.98] on all buttons (tactile feel) - Duration: 100ms (snappy) Loading State: - Replace text with spinner (Loader2 icon, animate-spin) - Maintain button width (min-w to prevent layout shift) - disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed Niche Mapping: Tech/Dev: Scale + Shadow (professional, satisfying) Creative/Agency: Gradient Shift or Fill Sweep (dramatic) Enterprise: Scale + Shadow only (conservative) AI/ML: Glow Effect + Scale (futuristic) E-commerce: Icon Animation (clear directional CTA) ``` **Best for:** All CTAs, navigation actions, form submissions **Niches:** All (select effect per niche mood) --- ## Section 4: Visual Effects Performance Rules ### Gradients - Max 3 gradient elements per viewport - CSS gradients only (never image gradients for solid colors) - Avoid gradient on gradient (visual noise) - Dark mode: reduce gradient intensity by 30-50% - `bg-gradient-to-br` preferred over radial for performance ### Glassmorphism (backdrop-blur) - **Hard limit: 5 elements with backdrop-blur per page** - Fallback: `@supports not (backdrop-filter: blur(12px)) { solid bg with opacity }` - Use `will-change: transform` on glass elements - Never stack glass on glass (blur compounds, GPU thrashes) - Mobile: reduce blur from `backdrop-blur-md` to `backdrop-blur-sm` ### Glow Effects - `box-shadow` with brand color at 15-25% opacity - Dark mode: increase to 20-30% (more visible) - Max 3 glow elements per viewport - Never animate box-shadow spread (expensive) -- only animate opacity ### Grain/Noise Textures - CSS-only using SVG filter: `url("data:image/svg+xml,...")` with `opacity-[0.03]` - Must not affect LCP (applied as pseudo-element, not on content) - Hide on `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` - Never use raster noise images (file size) ### General Rules - `will-change`: use sparingly, only on elements that actually animate - `contain: paint` on sections with heavy effects (prevent paint leak) - `transform: translate3d(0,0,0)` to force GPU layer (use for scroll animations) - `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: remove all transform-based animations, keep opacity-only transitions - Test on mid-range Android device (not just M-series MacBook)

input.content:
# Niche Blueprints -- Pixel's Section-by-Section Design System

> 3 complete blueprints (SaaS/Tech, E-commerce, AI/ML) + auto-research protocol for new niches.
> Each blueprint defines the full page structure, not just visual style.
> Load when designing landing pages or multi-page public sites.

---

## Blueprint Schema

Every niche blueprint follows this structure:

```
Niche:              Category name and description
Persona:            Primary target user (role, seniority, goals)
Design Anchors:     3-5 competitor references (what to channel, not copy)
Flowbase Blend:     Collection weights from mapping table
Animation Level:    Heavy / Moderate / Subtle / Minimal
Default Mode:       Dark / Light / System-adaptive
Color Direction:    Temperature, palette type, accent strategy
Typography:         Heading font, body font, mono font (from font-pairings.md)
Imagery:            Photography vs illustration vs abstract + style direction
Social Proof:       What types work best for this audience
Pricing UX:         Model type + psychological patterns
Interactive:        What interactive elements convert best
Section Order:      AIDA-adapted section sequence with rationale
```

---

## Blueprint 1: SaaS/Tech (B2B Developer Tools, Productivity, Infrastructure)

### Niche Profile

```
Niche:           SaaS/Tech -- B2B software, developer tools, productivity platforms, APIs
Persona:         Technical decision-makers, engineering managers, senior developers.
                 They evaluate quickly, respect craft, hate fluff. Want to see
                 the product, read the docs, check the pricing. 3-minute attention span.
Design Anchors:  Linear (polish + speed), Vercel (developer trust), Resend (clean + modern),
                 Supabase (open + technical), Dub.sh (minimal + effective)
Flowbase Blend:  Noda (40%) + Chalk (30%) + Aspect (30%)
Animation Level: Heavy -- tech audience expects and appreciates polish
Default Mode:    Dark (toggle available). Dark communicates "built by developers."
Color Direction: Cool-neutral base (zinc/slate). Accent: indigo, violet, or cyan.
                 Single accent color family. No warm tones.
Typography:      Geist Sans (headings) + Inter (body) + Geist Mono (code)
Imagery:         Product screenshots dominant. Terminal UIs, code editors, dashboards.
                 No stock photos. If illustration: isometric technical or abstract.
Social Proof:    GitHub stars, company logos ("trusted by X teams"), developer
                 testimonials (with GitHub avatar), usage metrics (requests/day, uptime %).
Pricing UX:      Usage-based highlighted, free tier prominent ("Start free, scale as you grow"),
                 3 tiers + enterprise. Show API call pricing clearly.
Interactive:     Code playground, API explorer, interactive docs preview
```

### Section Order (AIDA-Adapted)

| Order | Section | AIDA Phase | Purpose | Pattern |
|-------|---------|------------|---------|---------|
| 1 | Hero | Attention | Hook with value prop + product visual | Centered-gradient or Split |
| 2 | Social Proof Bar | Attention | Establish trust immediately | Logo strip + animated counters |
| 3 | Feature Bento Grid | Interest | Show capabilities at a glance | Bento Grid (3x3 or 2x3) |
| 4 | How It Works | Interest | Reduce complexity, show simplicity | 3-step horizontal flow |
| 5 | Product Demo | Desire | Let them experience the product | Code snippet + live output |
| 6 | Feature Deep-Dives | Desire | Detailed feature exploration | Asymmetric split (alternating) |
| 7 | Testimonials | Desire | Peer validation from developers | 3-card grid or carousel |
| 8 | Integrations | Desire | Show ecosystem compatibility | Logo grid with hover details |
| 9 | Pricing | Action | Convert interest to trial/purchase | 3-tier dark pricing + toggle |
| 10 | FAQ | Action | Handle objections | Accordion with schema.org |
| 11 | Final CTA | Action | Last conversion push | Gradient CTA section |
| 12 | Mega-Footer | -- | Navigation + newsletter | 5-column mega-footer |

### Section Specs

**1. Hero Section**

```
Layout: text-center max-w-4xl mx-auto
Background: dark with subtle radial gradient (primary/10 center, transparent edge)
Optional: grid dot pattern overlay at opacity-5

Components:
  - AnnouncementBadge: bg-primary/10 text-primary rounded-full px-3 py-1 text-sm
    Content: "New: [latest feature]" with arrow icon
  - H1 Heading: text-4xl md:text-5xl lg:text-6xl font-bold tracking-tight
    Gradient text option: bg-gradient-to-r from-white to-white/60 bg-clip-text
  - Subheading: text-lg md:text-xl text-muted-foreground max-w-2xl mx-auto mt-4
  - DualCTA: flex gap-4 justify-center mt-8
    Primary: bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/90 rounded-md px-6 py-3
    Secondary: border border-border text-foreground hover:bg-accent rounded-md px-6 py-3
  - ProductScreenshot: mt-12 rounded-xl border shadow-2xl shadow-primary/10
    Perspective transform: style={{ perspective: '1000px', transform: 'rotateX(2deg)' }}

Animation:
  Badge: fadeInUp, 200ms
  H1: fadeInUp, 400ms, delay 100ms
  Subheading: fadeInUp, 400ms, delay 200ms
  CTAs: fadeInUp, 300ms, delay 300ms
  Screenshot: fadeInUp, 500ms, delay 400ms + subtle float animation (continuous)

Dark Mode:
  Light: bg-white, dark text, screenshot with shadow
  Dark: bg-zinc-950, white text, screenshot with glow border
```

**2. Social Proof Bar**

```
Layout: flex items-center justify-center gap-8 md:gap-16 py-12
Background: transparent or bg-muted/30

Components:
  - Metrics (3-4): animated counters
    "10K+" developers | "99.9%" uptime | "50M+" API calls | "4.9" rating
  - Logo strip: grayscale logos, hover:grayscale-0 transition
    5-8 company logos in a row, opacity-40 hover:opacity-100

Animation: Counter roll-up 1500ms on scroll into view
Separator: border-r border-border between metrics (desktop only)
```

**3. Feature Bento Grid**

```
Layout: grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-4 md:gap-6
Cell sizing: 
  Row 1: span-2 (large feature) + span-1 (standard)
  Row 2: span-1 + span-1 + span-1
  Row 3: span-1 + span-2 (wide feature)

Card content:
  - Icon: w-10 h-10 rounded-lg bg-primary/10 text-primary p-2
  - Heading: text-lg font-semibold mt-4
  - Description: text-muted-foreground text-sm mt-2
  - Large cards: include mini code snippet or screenshot
  - Card bg: bg-card border rounded-xl p-6 hover:border-primary/30 transition

Animation: stagger entrance, 80ms delay between cards, fadeInUp
```

**4. How It Works**

```
Layout: grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-8 relative

Steps (3):
  - Step number: text-sm font-mono text-primary bg-primary/10 rounded-full w-8 h-8
  - Heading: text-lg font-semibold mt-4
  - Description: text-muted-foreground text-sm mt-2
  - Connecting line (desktop): absolute border-t-2 border-dashed border-border
    top-4 left-[calc(16.67%+20px)] right-[calc(16.67%+20px)]

Mobile: vertical stack with vertical connecting line on left side
```

**5. Product Demo**

```
Layout: max-w-4xl mx-auto
Content: tabbed code example with live output

Tab bar: flex gap-1 bg-muted/50 rounded-lg p-1
  Each tab: px-4 py-2 rounded-md text-sm
  Active: bg-background shadow-sm text-foreground
  Inactive: text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground

Code panel: bg-zinc-950 rounded-b-xl p-6 font-mono text-sm
  Syntax highlighting: keyword (text-purple-400), string (text-green-400),
  comment (text-zinc-500), function (text-blue-400)

Output panel: adjacent or below, showing the result of the code
```

**6-12: Follow patterns from flowbase-design-dna.md**
(Asymmetric split for deep-dives, testimonial carousel, integration grid, dark pricing, FAQ accordion, gradient CTA, mega-footer)

### Copy Framework for Quill

```json
{
  "niche": "SaaS/Tech",
  "voiceTone": "confident, technical, concise. Respect the reader's intelligence.",
  "avoid": "buzzwords (revolutionary, game-changing), exclamation marks, vague claims",
  "sections": {
    "hero": {
      "badge": { "maxWords": 3, "formula": "New: + Feature name", "tone": "factual" },
      "headline": { "maxWords": 8, "formula": "Action verb + Outcome", "tone": "direct, outcome-first" },
      "subheadline": { "maxWords": 25, "formula": "What it is + Who it's for + Key differentiator", "tone": "clear, specific" }
    },

    }
  }

```

---

## Blueprint 2: E-commerce (DTC Brands, Shopify, Marketplaces)

### Niche Profile

```
Niche:           E-commerce -- direct-to-consumer, Shopify stores, product marketplaces
Persona:         Store owners, merchandisers, marketing managers. They care about
                 conversion rates, average order value, and brand perception.
                 Visual-first, product-photography-dominant, mobile-heavy audience.
Design Anchors:  Shopify.com (platform authority), Allbirds (DTC craft), Glossier
                 (brand-forward), Gumroad (creator-friendly), Webflow (design quality)
Flowbase Blend:  Terrace (35%) + Breeze (35%) + Prism (30%)
Animation Level: Moderate -- product-focused, animations support browsing not distract
Default Mode:    Light (warm whites). Dark mode available but light-first.
Color Direction: Warm palette. Coral, amber, warm purple, sage green as accents.
                 Brand-forward -- product photos set the color tone.
                 Avoid cold corporate blues.
Typography:      Plus Jakarta Sans (headings) + Inter (body) + no mono needed
Imagery:         Product photography is KING. Lifestyle shots. User-generated content.
                 Studio product shots on clean backgrounds. Video product demos.
                 Never use generic stock. Photography > illustration always.
Social Proof:    Customer reviews (star ratings), "X customers served" counter,
                 Instagram/social embeds, press logos ("As seen in"), before/after photos
Pricing UX:      Consumer-friendly: prominent free tier or free trial. Price anchored
                 with "was $XX now $XX" if applicable. Annual discount toggle.
                 Money-back guarantee badge prominent.
Interactive:     Product configurator, size guide, color/variant selector, quick-view modal
```

### Section Order (AIDA-Adapted)

| Order | Section | AIDA Phase | Purpose | Pattern |
|-------|---------|------------|---------|---------|

## Auto-Research Protocol for New Niches

When Pixel encounters a niche not covered by the 3 core blueprints, follow this 7-step protocol to generate a custom blueprint on the fly.

### Step 1: Identify Niche Category

Map the product to the closest row in the niche-to-collection mapping table (flowbase-design-dna.md). If no row fits within 70% similarity, proceed to full auto-research.

### Step 2: Live Competitor Research

```
WebSearch queries (run all 3):
  1. "best [niche] landing pages 2026"
  2. "top [niche] SaaS websites design"
  3. "[competitor1] [competitor2] website" (if specific competitors known)

For each of top 5 results, WebFetch the landing page and extract:
  - Hero pattern (centered/split/video/screenshot/interactive)
  - Section count (how many sections before footer?)
  - Section order (what comes after hero?)
  - CTA style (button text, color, placement)
  - Animation level (none/subtle/moderate/heavy)
  - Social proof type (logos/reviews/metrics/case-studies/press)
  - Color temperature (warm/cool/neutral) + primary color family
  - Dark/light mode preference
  - Photography vs illustration usage
  - Typography style (geometric/humanist/serif/editorial)
  - Interactive elements present
```

### Step 3: Pattern Synthesis

Identify the 3 most common patterns across competitors:
- Most common hero pattern -> becomes default
- Most common section order -> becomes AIDA-adapted base
- Most common social proof type -> becomes primary proof strategy
- Average animation level -> becomes intensity setting

### Step 4: Flowbase Collection Mapping

Based on synthesized patterns, assign collection weights:
- Match color temperature to collection mood profiles
- Match animation level to collection animation characteristics
- Match typography style to collection typography direction
- Assign 40% / 30% / 30% weights to top 3 matching collections

### Step 5: Blueprint Generation

Use the blueprint schema to create a complete blueprint:
- Fill every field based on research findings
- Section order follows AIDA but adapted to niche conventions
- Copy framework follows niche voice/tone patterns
- Pricing UX matches niche pricing model expectations

### Step 6: Differentiation

Identify 1 intentional differentiator:
- What do ALL competitors do the same? -> Do it differently (but not worse)
- Examples: all use light mode -> consider dark. All use stock photos -> use custom illustration. All have 10+ sections -> try 7 focused sections.

### Step 7: Cache for Reuse

Write the generated blueprint to the project's `design-vision.md`:
```markdown
## Pixel Auto-Generated Blueprint
Niche: [name]
Generated: [date]
Competitors analyzed: [list]
Flowbase blend: [Primary] + [Secondary] + [Tertiary]
Section order: [list]
Differentiator: [what and why]
```

## Auto-Research Protocol for New Niches

When Pixel encounters a niche not covered by the 3 core blueprints, follow this 7-step protocol to generate a custom blueprint on the fly.

### Step 1: Identify Niche Category

Map the product to the closest row in the niche-to-collection mapping table (flowbase-design-dna.md). If no row fits within 70% similarity, proceed to full auto-research.

### Step 2: Live Competitor Research

```
WebSearch queries (run all 3):
  1. "best [niche] landing pages 2026"
  2. "top [niche] SaaS websites design"
  3. "[competitor1] [competitor2] website" (if specific competitors known)

For each of top 5 results, WebFetch the landing page and extract:
  - Hero pattern (centered/split/video/screenshot/interactive)
  - Section count (how many sections before footer?)
  - Section order (what comes after hero?)
  - CTA style (button text, color, placement)
  - Animation level (none/subtle/moderate/heavy)
  - Social proof type (logos/reviews/metrics/case-studies/press)
  - Color temperature (warm/cool/neutral) + primary color family
  - Dark/light mode preference
  - Photography vs illustration usage
  - Typography style (geometric/humanist/serif/editorial)
  - Interactive elements present
```

### Step 3: Pattern Synthesis

Identify the 3 most common patterns across competitors:
- Most common hero pattern -> becomes default
- Most common section order -> becomes AIDA-adapted base
- Most common social proof type -> becomes primary proof strategy
- Average animation level -> becomes intensity setting

### Step 4: Flowbase Collection Mapping

Based on synthesized patterns, assign collection weights:
- Match color temperature to collection mood profiles
- Match animation level to collection animation characteristics
- Match typography style to collection typography direction
- Assign 40% / 30% / 30% weights to top 3 matching collections

### Step 5: Blueprint Generation

Use the blueprint schema to create a complete blueprint:
- Fill every field based on research findings
- Section order follows AIDA but adapted to niche conventions
- Copy framework follows niche voice/tone patterns
- Pricing UX matches niche pricing model expectations

### Step 6: Differentiation

Identify 1 intentional differentiator:
- What do ALL competitors do the same? -> Do it differently (but not worse)
- Examples: all use light mode -> consider dark. All use stock photos -> use custom illustration. All have 10+ sections -> try 7 focused sections.

### Step 7: Cache for Reuse

Write the generated blueprint to the project's `design-vision.md`:
```markdown
## Pixel Auto-Generated Blueprint
Niche: [name]
Generated: [date]
Competitors analyzed: [list]
Flowbase blend: [Primary] + [Secondary] + [Tertiary]
Section order: [list]
Differentiator: [what and why]
```

Flag to Mira: "New niche blueprint generated for [niche]. Consider adding to permanent niche-blueprints.md if we build 2+ products in this space."

# CRO Psychology -- Pixel's Conversion Intelligence

> Conversion Rate Optimization patterns for public-facing pages.
> AIDA framework + social proof placement + pricing UX per niche.
> Phase 1: core framework. Phase 2: full pattern library.

---

## AIDA Section Ordering Framework

Every landing page follows the AIDA (Attention, Interest, Desire, Action) framework as its section ordering principle. Pixel adapts the specific sections per niche, but the psychological flow is constant.

```
ATTENTION (Sections 1-2):
  Goal: Stop the scroll. Capture attention in <3 seconds.
  Elements: Hero headline, visual hook, social proof hint
  Metric: Bounce rate < 40%

INTEREST (Sections 3-5):
  Goal: Educate. Show what the product does and why it matters.
  Elements: Feature grid, how-it-works, product demo
  Metric: Scroll depth > 50%

DESIRE (Sections 6-8):
  Goal: Create want. Show proof that it works for people like them.
  Elements: Testimonials, case studies, social proof, comparisons
  Metric: Time on page > 2 minutes

ACTION (Sections 9-12):
  Goal: Convert. Remove objections, present clear next step.
  Elements: Pricing, FAQ, final CTA, trust badges
  Metric: CTA click rate > 3%
```

### Niche-Specific AIDA Adaptations

| Niche | Attention Hook | Interest Focus | Desire Trigger | Action Driver |
|-------|---------------|----------------|----------------|---------------|
| SaaS/Tech | Product screenshot + metrics | Bento feature grid + code demo | Developer testimonials + GitHub stars | Free tier CTA + API docs link |
| E-commerce | Hero product photo + trust bar | Product showcase + benefits | Customer reviews + UGC | Buy CTA + money-back guarantee |
| AI/ML | Gradient hero + benchmark claim | Live playground + benchmark table | Enterprise logos + case metrics | Usage calculator + API key signup |
| Enterprise B2B | Authority headline + logo bar | Feature deep-dives + integrations | Case studies + ROI numbers | "Book demo" CTA + security badges |
| Developer Tools | Clean hero + "get started" code | Docs-style features + CLI demo | GitHub stars + community size | "npm install" CTA + docs link |

---

## Social Proof Placement Psychology

### Placement Rules (research-backed)

1. **Immediately after hero** (position 2): logo bar or metrics strip.
   Why: visitors who scroll past hero need immediate trust validation.

2. **Before pricing** (position n-3): testimonials or case studies.
   Why: social proof reduces price sensitivity. Always show proof before asking for money.

3. **Near primary CTA**: trust badges (security, guarantee, certification).
   Why: trust elements adjacent to action buttons increase click-through 12-15%.

4. **Above fold** (within hero): single metric or logo strip.
   Why: first impression trust. "Trusted by 10,000+ teams" in the hero reduces bounce.

### Social Proof Types by Niche

| Niche | Primary Proof | Secondary Proof | Placement Priority |
|-------|--------------|-----------------|-------------------|
| SaaS/Tech | Company logos | Developer testimonials | Logo bar after hero, testimonials before pricing |
| E-commerce | Star ratings + reviews | Customer count | Ratings in hero, reviews after product showcase |
| AI/ML | Benchmark numbers | Enterprise logos | Benchmarks in hero, logos before pricing |
| Enterprise | Case study ROI | Analyst recognition (Gartner, Forrester) | Case studies mid-page, badges near CTA |
| Developer Tools | GitHub stars + npm downloads | Community testimonials | Stars in hero, community before pricing |

### Social Proof Component Library

1. **Logo Bar:** 5-8 grayscale logos, hover:grayscale-0. "Trusted by X teams at..."
2. **Animated Counter Bar:** 3-5 metrics with count-up animation. "10K+ users | 99.9% uptime | 50M+ requests"
3. **Testimonial Cards:** Avatar + name + role + company + quote + stars. Grid or carousel.
4. **Case Study Teasers:** Company logo + metric highlight + 1-line result + "Read more" link.
5. **Trust Badge Row:** Security certs (SOC 2, GDPR), payment badges (Visa, Mastercard), guarantee badges.
6. **Press Bar:** "As seen in" + publication logos (TechCrunch, Product Hunt, etc.)
7. **Community Stats:** GitHub stars, Discord members, contributor count. With live-updating numbers.
8. **Before/After:** Visual comparison showing the product's impact. Slider or side-by-side.

---

## Pricing UX Patterns by Niche

### Developer Tools / API Products
```
Model: Usage-based primary, with flat-tier options
Layout: 3 tiers + enterprise
Key elements:
  - Free tier prominent ("Start free, no credit card")
  - Usage calculator interactive element
  - Per-unit pricing clearly shown (per API call, per request, per token)
  - "Most Popular" on mid-tier
  - Enterprise: "Contact Sales" with custom checkbox
CRO tactics:
  - Free tier reduces friction to zero
  - Calculator lets users self-serve pricing questions
  - Annual toggle with "Save 20%" badge
```

### Enterprise B2B
```
Model: Per-seat or flat-tier
Layout: 3 tiers, enterprise prominent
Key elements:
  - "Contact Sales" is the primary CTA (not self-serve)
  - ROI calculator ("Save X hours/month" based on team size)
  - Security/compliance badges near pricing
  - Custom enterprise features list
CRO tactics:
  - "Book a demo" > "Buy now" (longer sales cycle)
  - ROI calculator quantifies value before showing price
  - Compliance badges remove enterprise objections
```

### Consumer / SMB SaaS
```
Model: Flat-tier with annual discount
Layout: 3 tiers, free tier first
Key elements:
  - Free tier is generous (not a teaser)
  - "Most Popular" highlight on mid-tier
  - Monthly/Annual toggle with savings badge
  - Feature comparison table below cards
CRO tactics:
  - Price anchoring: show annual savings prominently
  - Decoy pricing: mid-tier looks best value relative to others
  - "No credit card required" reduces trial friction
```

### E-commerce / Marketplace
```
Model: Transaction-based or flat monthly
Layout: 2-3 tiers, volume-based
Key elements:
  - Transaction fees clearly shown
  - Volume discounts for higher tiers
  - "Pay as you grow" messaging
  - Money-back guarantee badge
CRO tactics:
  - Show revenue potential ("Earn $X/month with Y sales")
  - Free trial prominent
  - Success stories from similar-sized stores
```

---

## Above-Fold A/B Variant System

Every landing page gets 2-3 above-fold variants. Pixel outputs all variants; the team picks or A/B tests.

### Variant Templates

| Variant | Focus | Best When | Layout |
|---------|-------|-----------|--------|
| **Headline-First** | Strong value prop, text-dominant | Clear, differentiated value prop | Centered text, product screenshot below |
| **Visual-First** | Product screenshot/demo dominant | Product UI is impressive and self-explanatory | Split layout, image 50%+ of viewport |
| **Social-Proof-First** | Trust metrics above fold | Established product with strong numbers | Metrics bar above headline, logos below |

### A/B Test Output Format

```json
{
  "abTest": {
    "hypothesis": "Headline-first will outperform visual-first because [reason based on niche research]",
    "variants": [
      { "id": "A", "type": "headline-first", "description": "...", "priority": "control" },
      { "id": "B", "type": "visual-first", "description": "...", "priority": "challenger" },
      { "id": "C", "type": "social-proof-first", "description": "...", "priority": "stretch" }
    ],
    "successMetric": "CTA click-through rate",
    "minimumSampleSize": "1,000 visitors per variant",
    "expectedDuration": "2-4 weeks"
  }
}
```

# Page Type Library -- Pixel's 14 Public-Facing Page Types

> Every public-facing page type Pixel can design.
> Phase 1: definitions + critical sections. Phase 2: full section-by-section specs.
> Load when designing any page type beyond the landing page.

---

## Page Type Index

| # | Page Type | SEO Priority | CRO Focus | Complexity |
|---|-----------|-------------|-----------|------------|
| 1 | Landing Page | High | Primary conversion | High |
| 2 | About | Medium | Brand trust | Medium |
| 3 | Pricing | High | Revenue conversion | High |
| 4 | Blog Index | High | SEO + email capture | Medium |
| 5 | Blog Post | High | SEO + in-content CTA | Medium |
| 6 | Changelog | Low | Retention + re-engagement | Low |
| 7 | Careers | Medium | Talent acquisition | Medium |
| 8 | Contact | Medium | Lead capture | Low |
| 9 | Case Study | High | Sales enablement | Medium |
| 10 | Integrations | High | Feature discovery + SEO | Medium |
| 11 | Documentation | High | Developer conversion | High |
| 12 | 404 | Low | Recovery + navigation | Low |
| 13 | Coming Soon | Medium | Email list building | Low |
| 14 | Legal/Privacy | Low | Compliance | Low |

---

## Page Type Definitions

### 1. Landing Page

- **Purpose:** Primary conversion page. First impression. Must convert visitors to trial/signup/purchase.
- **Critical Sections:** Hero (with A/B variants), social proof bar, feature showcase, how-it-works, testimonials, pricing preview, CTA, mega-footer
- **SEO Priority:** High -- homepage and campaign landing pages drive organic traffic
- **CRO Elements:** A/B hero variants, social proof placement, pricing psychology, conversion-optimized CTA hierarchy
- **Spec:** Full specs in `niche-blueprints.md` (3 niche blueprints + auto-research)

### 2. About Page

- **Purpose:** Build trust, humanize the brand, tell the origin story. Secondary conversion path.
- **Critical Sections:** Mission statement hero, team grid (photos + roles), company timeline/milestones, values grid, investors/partners (if applicable), careers CTA
- **SEO Priority:** Medium -- ranks for "[brand] about" and "[brand] team"
- **CRO Elements:** Careers CTA for talent, investor logos for B2B trust, team photos for authenticity
- **Key Design Notes:** Photography-heavy (real team, not stock). Timeline can be horizontal (desktop) or vertical (mobile). Values section: icon + heading + description grid (3-4 values).

### 3. Pricing Page

- **Purpose:** Convert interest to purchase. Most revenue-critical page after landing.
- **Critical Sections:** Plan cards (3 tiers), feature comparison table, monthly/annual toggle, FAQ (objection handling), enterprise CTA, trust badges, money-back guarantee
- **SEO Priority:** High -- ranks for "[product] pricing" (high-intent keyword)
- **CRO Elements:** Price anchoring (most popular highlighted), annual discount toggle, feature comparison for decision support, trust badges near CTA, FAQ as objection handler
- **Key Design Notes:** See `cro-psychology.md` for niche-specific pricing UX patterns.

### 4. Blog Index

- **Purpose:** SEO traffic magnet + newsletter subscriber capture. Content hub.
- **Critical Sections:** Featured post hero, post grid/list, category filter/tabs, search, newsletter CTA (sidebar or inline), pagination or infinite scroll
- **SEO Priority:** High -- blog posts drive long-tail organic traffic
- **CRO Elements:** Newsletter CTA (above fold and inline), featured post highlight, category navigation for engagement depth
- **Key Design Notes:** Grid layout (2-3 columns) for visual blogs, list layout for text-heavy. Each card: featured image + title + excerpt + author + date + reading time + category badge.

### 5. Blog Post

- **Purpose:** Individual article page. SEO workhorse. In-content conversion.
- **Critical Sections:** Article hero (title + author + date + reading time), table of contents (sticky sidebar), article body (prose), author bio card, related posts grid, newsletter CTA, share buttons
- **SEO Priority:** High -- individual posts rank for specific keywords
- **CRO Elements:** In-article CTA (after 3rd paragraph or at 50% scroll), newsletter inline capture, related posts for engagement, sticky header with share + progress bar
- **Key Design Notes:** Max-width prose container (max-w-3xl). Clean typography with generous line-height. Code blocks with syntax highlighting if technical. Image optimization (WebP, lazy load).

### 6. Changelog

- **Purpose:** Show product momentum. Re-engage existing users. Build trust with prospects.
- **Critical Sections:** Version cards (date + title + description + tag), filter by category (feature/fix/improvement), subscribe for updates, latest version hero
- **SEO Priority:** Low -- mostly for existing users, not search traffic
- **CRO Elements:** "Try it now" CTA on each feature announcement, subscribe for updates email capture
- **Key Design Notes:** Timeline layout (vertical). Each entry: date badge + version tag + title + description + optional screenshot. Categories: feature (green), fix (yellow), improvement (blue).

### 7. Careers Page

- **Purpose:** Attract talent. Show company culture. Convert visitors to applicants.
- **Critical Sections:** Culture hero (mission + team photo/video), open positions list (filterable by department/location), benefits grid, team testimonials, office gallery, application CTA per position
- **SEO Priority:** Medium -- ranks for "[company] careers" and "[company] jobs"
- **CRO Elements:** Clear "Apply Now" per position, benefits grid (what makes this job great), team quotes for authenticity, easy application flow (minimal fields)
- **Key Design Notes:** Positions grouped by department with expand/collapse. Each position card: title + department + location + type (full-time/remote) + "Apply" button. Benefits: icon + title + description grid.

### 8. Contact Page

- **Purpose:** Lead capture. Support access. Make the company reachable.
- **Critical Sections:** Contact form (name + email + subject + message), office information (address + map), alternative contact methods (email, phone, social), FAQ section for self-service, response time expectation
- **SEO Priority:** Medium -- ranks for "[company] contact"
- **CRO Elements:** Simple form (4-5 fields max), clear response time ("We reply within 24h"), alternative channels for urgency, FAQ to deflect common questions
- **Key Design Notes:** Split layout: form on left (60%), contact info on right (40%). Map embed optional but effective. Include department-specific emails if applicable.

### 9. Case Study

- **Purpose:** Sales enablement. Prove ROI. Convert enterprise prospects.
- **Critical Sections:** Company hero (logo + name + industry + challenge), challenge/solution/results narrative, key metrics highlight (3-4 big numbers), customer quote, related case studies, CTA (book demo / start trial)
- **SEO Priority:** High -- ranks for "[product] case study" and industry-specific queries
- **CRO Elements:** Big metric numbers (animated counters), customer quote with attribution, "Get similar results" CTA, industry/size filter for relevance
- **Key Design Notes:** Storytelling structure: Challenge > Solution > Results. Metrics section: 3-4 large numbers in a row ("+73% efficiency", "-40% costs", "2x faster"). Include company logo and industry tag for credibility.

### 10. Integrations Page

- **Purpose:** Show ecosystem compatibility. Drive feature discovery. SEO for "[product] + [integration]" keywords.
- **Critical Sections:** Integration hero (count + search), partner logo grid (filterable by category), individual integration detail cards, featured integrations section, "Request an integration" CTA
- **SEO Priority:** High -- each integration creates a keyword-targeted page ("[product] [integration] integration")
- **CRO Elements:** Search/filter for quick discovery, featured integrations for popular tools, "Request an integration" for engagement, individual integration pages for SEO
- **Key Design Notes:** Logo grid with category tabs (CRM, Email, Analytics, etc.). Each logo: hover card with integration name + description + "Learn more" link. Individual pages: overview + setup guide + features + CTA.

### 11. Documentation Page

- **Purpose:** Developer conversion. Self-serve onboarding. Reduce support load.
- **Critical Sections:** Sidebar navigation (collapsible sections), search (global), content area (markdown/MDX), code examples (multi-language tabs), "On this page" table of contents, feedback widget, prev/next navigation
- **SEO Priority:** High -- documentation pages are high-intent SEO magnets for developers
- **CRO Elements:** "Get started" prominent in nav, code copy buttons, API key signup inline, feedback widget for engagement
- **Key Design Notes:** 3-column layout on desktop: sidebar nav (fixed) + content (scrollable) + "On this page" ToC (fixed). Code blocks: multi-language tabs (Python, JavaScript, cURL), copy button, syntax highlighting. Mobile: sidebar becomes hamburger menu.

### 12. 404 Page

- **Purpose:** Recovery. Help lost visitors find what they need. Reduce exit rate.
- **Critical Sections:** Error illustration/animation, error message (friendly, not technical), search bar, popular links / suggested pages, homepage CTA
- **SEO Priority:** Low -- should return 404 status code (no indexing)
- **CRO Elements:** Search bar for recovery, popular page links, homepage CTA, optional humorous illustration for brand personality
- **Key Design Notes:** Centered layout. Illustration should match brand personality (playful for consumer, clean for enterprise). Message: "This page doesn't exist" not "404 Error." Include breadcrumbs or site map link.

### 13. Coming Soon Page

- **Purpose:** Email list building. Generate pre-launch buzz. Validate interest.
- **Critical Sections:** Product name/logo, value proposition headline, email capture form, countdown timer (if launch date known), social links, optional: feature preview or waitlist position counter
- **SEO Priority:** Medium -- captures "[product name]" searches before launch
- **CRO Elements:** Email capture is the sole goal. Countdown creates urgency. "Join X others on the waitlist" for social proof. Early-bird incentive if applicable.
- **Key Design Notes:** Single-page, no navigation. Full-viewport hero. Background: gradient, abstract pattern, or brand-relevant imagery. Email input + submit button centered. Minimal distractions -- one action only.

### 14. Legal/Privacy Page

- **Purpose:** Compliance. Build trust through transparency. Required by law.
- **Critical Sections:** Table of contents (clickable anchors), last updated date, clean prose sections (numbered), contact information for privacy inquiries
- **SEO Priority:** Low -- but must be crawlable and accessible
- **CRO Elements:** None -- this page is purely informational. Clean, readable design builds trust.
- **Key Design Notes:** Max-width prose container (max-w-3xl). Generous line-height for readability. Numbered sections with anchor links. "Last updated: [date]" prominent at top. Sticky table of contents sidebar on desktop. Print-friendly styles.

---
